questions.q: What is online reputation management for franchises?
questions.a: It's the process of monitoring, responding to and acting on reviews and feedback across every franchise location and platform. That includes Google, Yelp, TripAdvisor and delivery apps like DoorDash. For franchises, the challenge is doing it consistently at scale while keeping one brand voice across many owners.

questions.q: Which review platforms should a restaurant franchise manage?
questions.a: Google Business Profile comes first, because your rating there affects how often you show up in local search and Google Maps. Yelp, TripAdvisor, Facebook, DoorDash and OpenTable each matter for different guests and restaurant types. Delivery app ratings also affect how visible you are inside those apps.

questions.q: How can franchisees keep a consistent brand voice when replying to reviews?
questions.a: Give every location a shared response framework with brand-approved tone and examples for positive, negative and fake reviews. Encourage personal touches, like using the guest's name and mentioning something specific from their review. A central tool that suggests on-brand replies helps local teams respond quickly without drifting from the brand voice.

questions.q: What metrics should I track for franchise reputation?
questions.a: Track average star rating by platform and location, review volume, response rate and average response time. Sentiment, NPS, negative review rate and guest recovery rate show what's behind the stars. Compare each location with nearby competitors so a strong portfolio average doesn't hide a struggling store.

questions.q: How do I turn franchise reviews into operational improvements?
questions.a: Tag reviews by operational area, such as food quality, wait times, order accuracy, staff and cleanliness, then track the tags by location. Look for repeated complaints and match their timing against shift data to find the cause. Share the patterns with operations, kitchen and marketing teams so each can act on what applies to them.

questions.q: Is there software to manage reputation across franchise locations?
questions.a: Yes, reputation management platforms pull reviews from every location and platform into one place. Momos, for example, uses AI to categorize reviews by topic, show which locations are underperforming and why, and surface recurring issues before they spread. Its AI Review Manager also replies to reviews around the clock from a Unified Inbox.
